title: VNI Synthetic Practice Test
description: A synthetic four-module paper written for this repository. Every passage, prompt, option and answer here is invented; none of it is Cambridge material and none of it is intended as IELTS practice. It exists so a clean checkout can run the exam engine end to end without depending on content whose licence nobody has established. THE BAND TABLES BELOW ARE INVENTED TOO — they cover the raw range so the reader accepts the package, and they are not equated to anything. Where VNI's real tables come from is H-4, still open, and no band produced from this paper may be shown to a learner.

parts.title: Surveying the Lower Delta
parts.body:
In the spring of the survey's second year the team returned to the lower delta with three instruments and a fortnight of daylight. The river had moved since the previous visit — not far, but far enough that the marks cut into the northern bank no longer stood where the earlier maps put them.

Work began with depth. A sounding line, weighted and marked at half-metre intervals, was dropped from the launch at fixed points across the channel, and the readings were entered by hand before the boat had drifted. It is slow work and it is the only measurement the team trusted without a second opinion.

Flow was harder. The meter had been calibrated in a laboratory tank and the delta is not a tank; the first dawn readings disagreed with the afternoon ones by more than the instrument's stated tolerance, and the team went back to the northern bank to recalibrate rather than record a number they could not defend. The fortnight ran out four days before the survey was finished.

parts.body:
The table below shows the number of visitors to four public libraries in one city over three years. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

| Library | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Central | 82,000 | 79,000 | 71,000 |
| Riverside | 24,000 | 31,000 | 44,000 |
| Hilltop | 18,000 | 17,000 | 17,500 |
| Eastgate | 9,000 | 14,000 | 22,000 |

Some people believe a city should spend its cultural budget on a small number of large institutions; others believe it should be spread across many small local venues.

Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

parts.title: Introduction and interview
parts.body:
Let's talk about where you live.

· Do you live in a house or an apartment?
· What do you like most about the area you live in?
· Has it changed much since you moved there?
· Would you like to live somewhere else one day? (Why?)

questions.prompt: Answer the examiner's questions about where you live.

questions.prompt: Speak for one to two minutes on the topic on the card.

parts.title: Two-way discussion
parts.body:
We've been talking about a journey that did not go as planned. Now let's consider travel more generally.

· Why do people find delays so frustrating?
· Should transport operators be required to compensate passengers?
· Do you think people travelled more patiently in the past?

questions.prompt: Discuss the examiner's questions about travel.
